Filter Nesting Attempts to the Active Nesting Period

Source: R/nw.filteractive.R
nw.filteractive.Rd

Trimming nesting attempt checks to the active periods (nest contains or likely contains host or brood parasite eggs and/or chicks) may provide better pictures of nest start and end dates. Knowing nest active dates can be useful when calculating nest exposure days as well as comparing changes in the nesting period over space and time. This function notes individual nest checks within an attempt if no eggs or chicks of either host or parasite species are recorded (in numbers, as present, or likely present (i.e. an adult is on the nest and was not flushed)). This differs slightly from nw.filterphenology's trim_to_active = T argument where build is considered active in the whole nest phenologic cycle and automatically included the fail/fledge check where the first 0 eggs/young are recorded after being positive. See details below.

Usage

nw.filteractive(data, mode, include_ffcheck = FALSE, output = NULL)

Arguments

data

dataframe; A dataframe of merged NestWatch attempt and visits data. Date columns must have class Date and Datetime columns must have class POSIXct.

mode

"flag" or "remove"; A character string defining if the analyst wants the identified nesting attempts to be flagged with "FLAGGED" in a new column, or removed from the dataset.

include_ffcheck

logical; TRUE or FALSE indicating whether the fledge/fail check (first 0 eggs/young recorded after last positive count) should be retained (not flagged or removed). Though the nest is inactive, retaining this may allow more estimation of fledge/fail dates closer to the true, unobserved date. Defaults set to FALSE.

output

character; An optional character string to custom name the output dataframe.

Value

dataframe

Details

This function summarizes by nest check, if eggs or chicks were counted or present, or if there is evidence of adult behavior indicative of eggs or chicks being present but not visible in the nest. If evidence of eggs or chicks are not present, the check is noted as not active. This function then flags (or removes) the leading and trailing checks noted as inactive. If a check is noted as inactive, but occur between two active checks, that check will not be flagged – this usually occurs when a participant has not recorded full data for that check, like in cases where an adult was present but eggs/chicks were not looked for. This method flags (or removes) the last "fail/fledge check", as the contents of the nest in that case are usually 0. This function also does not account for nests being failed by abandonment or partial predation, as there would still be a record of eggs being present despite the nest having failed (knowingly or unknowingly by the participant). This function contrasts with nw.filterphenology's trim_to_active = T argument, where in the latter only host eggs/young are considered, the "fail/fledge" check (first 0 egg/chick count after a positive count) is retained automatically, checks prior to eggs/young are retained if a nest is incomplete or complete (suspected to be in build), and a species-specific phenology table is used to identify period of unacceptable length (such as long in incubation may suggest abandonment).

Examples

# Simplified NestWatch dataset with nest summary dates
# Checks 1 & 5 should be flagged as inactive (no eggs/young/or adults on the nest)
data <- data.frame(Attempt.ID = c("A1", "A1", "A1", "A1", "A1"),
                  Species.Code = rep("carwre", 5),
                  # simulate data for four visits to one nest
                  Visit.Datetime = c(as.POSIXct(rep(NA, 5))),
                  Visit.ID = c("S001", "S002", "S003", "S004", "S005"),
                  Visit.Datetime = as.POSIXct(c("2024-05-01", "2024-05-05",
                                                "2024-05-08", "2024-05-15", "2024-05-18")),
                  Adult.Activity = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA),
                  Host.Eggs.Count = c(0, 2, 0, 2, 0),
                  Host.Eggs.Present.Uncounted = rep(NA, 5),
                  Brood.Parasite.Eggs.Count = c(0, 0, NA, 0, 0),
                  Brood.Parasite.Eggs.Present.Uncounted = c(0, 0, NA, 0, 0),
                  Live.Host.Young.Present.Uncounted = rep(NA, 5),
                  Live.Host.Young.Count = c(0, 0, NA, 0, 0),
                  Brood.Parasite.Live.Young.Count = c(0, 0, NA, 0, 0),
                  Brood.Parasite.Live.Young.Present.Uncounted = c(0, 0, NA, 0, 0),
                  Nest.Status = rep(NA, 5))

out <- nw.filteractive(data = data, mode = "flag")
#> ... Identified nesting attempts have been noted with 'FLAGGED' in the in column 'Flagged.Check'.
